subject: truck2077
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: futuristic militarized truck from 2077.
Style: low-poly cyberpunk, extremely intricate.
reasoning:
I'm deciding this can be a static model without joints, keeping the geometry simple in model space, and planning out a 6x6 military truck's rough dimensions facing forward.

I'm sketching the wheel layout across three axles, chassis frame, armored cab with a glowing cyan windshield slit, a roof turret railgun, cargo bed with missile pods, and decal textures, while working out precise coordinates so wheels sit flush on the ground and the hull panels align correctly.

Continuing the windshield slope down to the roofline, I check the total cab height with turret comes to about 3.9, which works fine. I verify the extrusion axes so the cab thickness runs correctly along x, then move to adding a glowing quad on the windshield slope for visual effect.

For the windshield plane, I'm computing its normal, placement, and size to fit the slope angle, adding a gradient texture with HUD lines and a glow effect. Then I add small dark cyan side windows positioned symmetrically at the cab's half-width, and plan hood details like vents and lights.

Next I'm adding a front bumper box, angled bull bar plates, glowing headlight boxes near the top, and thin neon underglow strips along the sides in cyan with magenta glow accents. For the cargo section, I'm sizing an armored rear container box positioned to sit flush on top of the hull.

Now I'm working out the roof-mounted missile pod rack: two launcher pods positioned symmetrically, each containing a 3x2 grid of short angled cylinder tubes tilted upward around the x-axis, computing offset positions for each tube within the pod rather than merging geometry.

Then I'm adding a cab-roof turret with a ring base, sloped body box, and twin railgun barrels extending forward with glowing cyan coil rings wrapped around them.

For the container, I'm planning side decals like a hex emblem, "UNIT 77" text, hazard stripes, dark rear doors with light line details, and red glowing rear lights. For the wheels, I'm sketching dark tires with metal hubs, a thin glowing cyan rim ring, and a few lug bolts.

Writing wheel geometry code...

Now I'm adding mudguards as boxes positioned over each wheel axle, plus hub-guard side skirts, and planning vertical exhaust stacks behind the cab near the sides.

Then I'm sketching accessories: antennas with glowing tips, a roof light bar, spotlights, side fuel tanks between the axles, toolboxes, angled armor plates on the cab sides, a rooftop radar dish built from a flipped cone and a partial hemisphere for a satellite dish, plus roof sensor domes and vents, before moving on to texturing considerations.

Now I'm planning the SVG textures I'll need: a hex emblem with a wolf/eye motif, hazard stripes, a HUD windshield overlay, stencil text reading something like "MK-IX / WARDOG 2077", and a neon sign using safer Latin text like "NEXUS" instead of risky CJK characters, roughly six textures total. I'm also settling on a dark gunmetal and olive camo base paint with magenta/cyan neon and yellow hazard accents, mixing mottled olive tones and camo patch colors for the hull material.

I'm working out helper functions for building box and extrude geometry without needing bones or joints, since static models can skip rigging entirely. I'm planning to use flat shading for the boxes, apply the hull paint to the extruded cab, build angled slab armor instead of complex wedges, write a symmetry helper to mirror parts left-right, and use a textured plane for the windshield decal so it carries its own tinted artwork.

Now I'm reasoning through the orientation math for placing emblem decals on the container's side panels, working out which way the plane should face and how the local axes map to world space so the text reads correctly when mirrored to the opposite side.

Then I'm sketching out the hull and container box dimensions and positions, working out the center coordinates and sizes so the pieces line up properly.

Now I'm planning the front bumper and bull bar details, positioning an angled wedge plate, winch glow, and grille elements near the front of the vehicle.

Now I'm working out the hood profile and adding a scoop with vents, then positioning the three wheel sets along the z-axis and checking fender clearance against the container hull and wheel widths.

Adding decorative side flares, an axle rod connecting the wheels, neon underglow strips in cyan and magenta along the container, and planning missile pods and a turret ring on the cab roof.

Finishing the turret with its body, mantlet, and dual railgun barrels extending forward, confirming the roof geometry supports the overhang and sets total vehicle height. I'm also adding a mirrored light bar on the cab roof slope and exhaust stacks with glowing orange tips at the rear.

Now I'm placing antennas with glowing tips near the rear, rear lighting with a red glow, a hitch and bumper, and working out side detail placement for toolboxes between the wheels given the hull's wheel spacing.

I'm fitting cylindrical side tanks with cyan glow bands into the gap between the front and mid wheel wells, then adding angular armor panels and sensor domes to the container sides, plus scattered vents and rivets for extra greeble detail.

Now I'm designing a hexagonal emblem with a magenta ring and chevron visor shape, labeled "77" in monospace font, and planning hand-drawn hazard stripe polygons for the bumpers rather than relying on SVG patterns. I'm keeping the color palette tight—around 25 flat color strings—and importing glow and metal/panel helpers from the kit libraries to keep the file近 400 lines.

Writing wheel geometry...

Adding side window planes and checking their geometry against the cab slope, then planning thin dark door seam lines and handles.
